source.title: The Readout Shortcut: Positional Number Copying Dominates Arithmetic CoT Readout in Small Language Models

page_placements.theme: Identifying induction heads: scores miss heads or diverge from causal role

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures induction-score overlap with heads associated with arithmetic CoT copying, using a different method from testing induction-head formation or the original repeated-token behavior.
record.gate_note: The paper's main experiments concern positional copying of numbers in arithmetic CoT readout, not the repeated-token induction behavior or in-context-learning training dynamics in the claim. The relevant results are the exploratory induction-score and copy-head-overlap analyses in Appendix P.
record.test_reason: The study's subject is positional copying of the trailing number in arithmetic CoT readout by 1–3B instruction-tuned GQA models. Induction heads enter only in exploratory Appendix P. There, an Olsson-style induction score (prefix-matching × copying on repeated random-token sequences) is used as a tool to characterise the study's own copy-sensitive heads, through top-20 overlap and rank correlations. None of these results bears on the versions. They do not show whether induction heads compose with previous-token heads in small attention-only models (V1), how heads form during training (V2, V5, V7), or what role induction heads play in in-context learning (V3, V6). Nor do they report how widespread induction heads are across families (V4). Only one per-model induction score is given: Gemma's top head, 0.44.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors describe a gradient from convergent (Gemma) through partial (Llama) to diffuse (Qwen) in induction/copy-head overlap. They call the analysis exploratory, with uncorrected p-values. They present head analyses as sensitivity profiles, not complete circuits, with the behavioural copy results as primary evidence.
record.recipe_differences: Uses induction-score measurements and overlap with arithmetic CoT copy-sensitive head rankings; it does not reproduce induction-head formation or measure the original repeated-token task.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported induction/copy overlap varies by architecture; Qwen's ranking association also differs by comparator.

fits_no_version.finding: Heads ranked by induction score overlap the arithmetic-CoT copy-sensitive heads significantly in Gemma (7/20) and Llama (5/20), but only at chance in Qwen (2/20, ρ=0.046 vs. the patching ranking).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Heads that copy the answer number in arithmetic CoT readout coincide with induction heads in some architectures but not others.

record.problems: The induction-overlap analysis is exploratory and uses uncorrected p-values. Head overlap and score correlations do not establish causal composition with a previous-token head or the canonical induction behavior.
record.rows_left_out: Main arithmetic readout, shuffle, scaling, and training results were not included because they do not measure induction-head behavior or the claim's ICL/training-transition versions.

untested.parts: Previous-token-head composition and [A][B]…[A]→[B] completion in small attention-only transformers. The models are 1–3B GQA LLMs. A previous-token-head check is said to be released with the code, but no result is reported.
All parts: no in-context learning measured by loss over token index.
Induction scores are computed in three families, but presence or prevalence is not reported. Only Gemma's top score (0.44) is given.
All parts: few-shot task learning is not studied.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' with V1 labels over-reaches. Overlap between induction-score heads and task-specific copy heads does not test the induction mechanism. The models are also not small attention-only transformers. The overlap analysis is exploratory and uses uncorrected p-values. The previous-token-head check is only mentioned as released with the code.

versions.untested_parts: Does not directly test previous-token-head composition, canonical [A][B] … [A] → [B] completion, or induction-head formation during training; models are instruction-tuned GQA language models, not described as attention-only transformers.

The paper reports induction-score overlap across three model architectures, but does not test whether induction-behavior heads appear across families, sizes, training runs, architectures, or modalities.

That is a related construct, not induction behaviour or its mechanism in small attention-only transformers. The value mixes the overlap (7/20, p=9.2e-4) with Gemma's top induction score (L18H6, 0.44). L18H6 is also Gemma's top attention-mass copy head (Appendix A).

relation.reason: The study uses induction-head measurements to characterize its copy-sensitive heads without testing formation, training transitions, or induction heads' contribution to in-context learning.

tranche.reason: Induction scoring serves as a diagnostic tool for arithmetic-readout head overlap; the reported overlap results do not test a claim version.

source_check.notes: The recipe incorrectly says the study does not measure the repeated-token task: Appendix P explicitly measures prefix matching and copying on repeated random-token sequences. The overlap analyses are exploratory with uncorrected p-values and do not establish complete circuits.
